title: Wedding Vow Examples: 26 Heartfelt Vows to Inspire Your Own
h1: Wedding Vow Examples: 26 Heartfelt, Funny and Short Vows to Inspire Your Own
description: Browse 26 wedding vow examples, from traditional and romantic to short, funny and blended-family vows, plus a simple formula for writing your own with ease.
excerpt: Stuck on your vows? Browse 26 wedding vow examples — traditional, romantic, short, funny and more — and use our simple formula to write your own.
intro:
Writing your own vows is one of the most meaningful parts of planning a wedding, and one of the most intimidating. How do you fit everything you feel into a couple of minutes, in front of everyone you love, without crying through every word (or maybe while crying through every word)?

This guide gives you a simple structure for personal vows and 26 wedding vow examples to borrow from: traditional, modern romantic, short, funny, for blended families and nonreligious ceremonies. Treat them as starting points. The best vows sound like the two of you, so swap in your real stories, names and promises wherever you can.
body:
A simple formula for writing your vows

Most memorable vows follow a loose four-part shape. You do not have to use all four, but it is a reliable way to get unstuck:

  1. Open with them. Say your partner's name and something true about who they are or what they mean to you.
  2. Share a moment. A short story: when you met, when you knew, a time they showed up for you. Keep it to two or three sentences.
  3. Make your promises. Three to six specific promises, ideally a mix of serious and lighthearted.
  4. Close with a line of commitment. Something like “I choose you, today and every day.”

Aim for one to two minutes when spoken aloud, roughly 150 to 300 words. Coordinate with your partner on length and tone so one set of vows is not three times longer or much more formal than the other.

Tip: Before you start writing, jot down answers to three questions: When did you know? What do you love most about who they are? What do you want your marriage to feel like? Your vows are hiding in those answers.

Traditional wedding vow examples

Classic vows are timeless for a reason. Many couples use a traditional base and add a personal sentence or two.

I take you to be my partner in marriage, to have and to hold from this day forward, for better, for worse, for richer, for poorer, in sickness and in health, to love and to cherish, as long as we both shall live.

I promise to be true to you in good times and in bad, in sickness and in health. I will love you and honor you all the days of my life.

With this ring, I give you my heart, my faithfulness and my love. From this day forward, wherever you go, I will go, and whatever comes, we will face it together.

Before our families and friends, I take you as my husband. I promise to stand beside you, to share your joys and your burdens and to love you faithfully for the rest of my life.

Modern romantic vow examples

[Name], the first time you laughed at one of my terrible jokes, I knew I wanted to spend my life trying to make you laugh. You have been my safe place, my biggest cheerleader and my favorite adventure. I promise to listen even when I want to argue, to hold your hand in waiting rooms and on roller coasters, and to keep choosing you every single day. You are my home.

I didn't believe in “the one” until I met you. Then suddenly every song made sense. I promise to love you when it's easy and especially when it's hard. I promise to celebrate your wins louder than my own, to give you space when you need it and to always come back to you. Today I give you all of me, and I can't wait to see who we become together.

You make ordinary days feel like something worth remembering: Sunday pancakes, late-night drives, the way you hum while you cook. I promise to keep noticing those moments. I promise to be honest, to be kind even when I'm tired and to never stop being curious about you. I love who you are, and I love who I am with you.

When life got hard last year, you didn't flinch. You stayed, you held on and you made me laugh when I thought I couldn't. That's when I knew. I promise to be that person for you. I promise to show up, to stay and to love you through every season. You are my best friend, and today you become my family.

I promise to love you not just as you are today, but as you grow and change. I promise to be your partner in every dream, your shelter in every storm and your loudest fan in every room. I've loved you for years, and I'm ready to love you for the rest of my life.

[Name], you are the calm to my chaos and the courage to my doubt. I promise to make our home a place of laughter and safety. I promise to apologize first, forgive quickly and never go to bed without saying “I love you.” Today I give you my hand, my heart and my forever.

Short and sweet vow examples

Perfect for elopements, small ceremonies or anyone who would rather keep it brief.

I choose you. Today, tomorrow and every day after. In joy and in struggle, I'm yours.

You are my best friend and my greatest love. I promise to stand by you, believe in you and make you laugh for as long as we live.

I promise to love you when it's easy, fight for us when it's hard and always find my way back to you.

Wherever you are is where I want to be. I give you my heart, today and always.

I promise to be your partner, your safe place and your biggest fan. I love you, and I always will.

Funny wedding vow examples

Humor works best when it is balanced with sincerity. Aim for one or two laughs, then land on something heartfelt.

I promise to love you, honor you and pretend not to notice when you eat the last slice of pizza. I promise to share the remote, the blankets and, on special occasions, my fries. Most of all, I promise to laugh with you through everything life throws at us, because there's no one I'd rather be ridiculous with.

I vow to always tell you when you have something in your teeth, to never start a show without you (even the good ones) and to accept that you will always be right about directions. But mostly, I vow to love you fiercely and choose you every day.

I promise to tolerate your 47 alarms every morning, to listen to your full-length dog stories and to keep the snack drawer stocked. In return, I ask only that you keep loving me as much as you love our dog. On second thought, 80 percent is fine.

Before I met you, I had a very organized life. Now I have a partner who leaves cabinet doors open and a heart that has never been happier. I promise to close the cabinets, to keep making you coffee and to love you through every messy, wonderful year.

Vows for blended families and second marriages

[Name], I promise to love you, and I promise to love and support [child's name] as part of the family we're creating. I will be patient as we grow together, respectful of the bonds that came before me and present for every school play, scraped knee and late-night talk.

We both know life doesn't always go as planned. That's what makes this moment so precious. I come to you with a full heart and hard-won wisdom. I promise to never take our love for granted, to keep talking even when it's hard and to build a home where everyone feels safe.

To [child's name]: today I'm not only marrying your parent, I'm promising to be someone you can count on. I'll listen, I'll show up and I'll always respect who you are. We're becoming a family, and I'm grateful you're part of it.

Nonreligious and interfaith vow examples

In front of the people who shaped us, I promise to honor your beliefs and traditions as I honor my own. I promise to build a home with room for both of our histories and to create new traditions together.

I promise to be your partner in all things: to respect your independence, nurture our connection and build a life rooted in kindness, honesty and laughter. I choose you freely and completely.

I don't need a script to tell you how I feel. I love you. I trust you. I want to build a life with you. I promise to keep showing you that with my actions, every day.

Today we promise each other a lifetime of honesty, patience and adventure. I will hold your hand through the unknown and celebrate every ordinary day with you as the gift that it is.

How to deliver your vows with confidence

  • Practice out loud several times, ideally in front of a mirror or a trusted friend who will keep it a secret.
  • Print them nicely. A small vow book or card looks better in photos than your phone.
  • Slow down. Nerves make everyone speak fast. Pause after key lines.
  • Look up. Glance at your partner often, especially for your promises.
  • Let the emotion happen. If your voice cracks, take a breath and keep going. It is one of the most moving parts of a wedding.
  • Hand your officiant a backup copy in case anything gets lost.
Tip: Avoid inside jokes that only one or two guests will understand, and skip any stories your partner might find embarrassing. When in doubt, ask yourself: “Would they smile hearing this in front of their grandmother?”

Keep the promises going after the wedding

Your vows do not have to stay in a drawer. Many couples reread them on anniversaries or frame them at home. For words to share in the years ahead, browse our anniversary wishes for husband and wife, write one of our I love you letters on your first anniversary, or find the perfect post with our wedding captions for Instagram. You can explore more in our wedding advice section.
takeaways: Use a simple shape: open with your partner, share a moment, make promises, close with commitment.
Aim for one to two minutes and coordinate length and tone with your partner.
Balance humor with sincerity and skip inside jokes most guests won't get.
Practice out loud, print your vows and give your officiant a backup copy.

faq.q: How long should wedding vows be?
faq.a: Most personal vows take one to two minutes to read aloud, which is roughly 150 to 300 words. That is long enough to share a story and a few promises without losing your guests. Agree on a similar length with your partner so your vows feel balanced.

faq.q: What do you say in wedding vows?
faq.a: Personal vows usually include your partner's name, something you love about them, a brief story about your relationship and several specific promises for your marriage. Many end with a line of commitment, such as choosing them today and every day. Traditional vows focus on lifelong faithfulness.

faq.q: Is it okay to use wedding vow examples?
faq.a: Yes. Many couples start from traditional vows or examples and personalize them with their own stories and promises. Borrowing a structure or a favorite line is completely fine. The key is adding details that make the vows unmistakably about the two of you.

faq.q: Should we share our vows with each other before the wedding?
faq.a: It is a personal choice. Some couples love the surprise; others share them in advance or ask the officiant to review both sets so length and tone match. A middle ground is agreeing on a word count and style without reading each other's actual vows.
